events.description: In 1964, ITV broadcast a film about 14 seven-year-olds, which became the longest-running documentary series ever. It set out to prove that Britain was divided by the class system and that these children's futures had been decided by the street they were born on. This programme looks at the year 7 Up was made, the idea behind it, and what the subjects hoped for in a Britain about to change around them

events.name: Gary Barlow's Food and Wine Tour: New Zealand
events.description: Gary and Jason Manford head to Havelock, gateway to the Marlborough Sounds, where local seafood entrepreneur Maegan Blom takes them through a spectacular maze of sheltered waterways, forested hills and peaceful bays. They drop anchor at her working mussel farm to see how greenshell mussels are grown, before heading back to shore for meal. Then they drive their camper van to Picton to board a ferry for the scenic Cook Strait crossing from the South Island to the North Island, heading up to the bridge to meet the captain, before enjoying a sunny beer-tasting out on deck

With analysis from Ian Wright, Roy Keane and Juan Mata, commentary by Sam Matterface and Lee Dixon, and interviews from Gabriel Clarke

They drop anchor at her working mussel farm to see how greenshell mussels are grown, before heading back to shore for meal. Then they drive their camper van to Picton to board a ferry for the scenic Cook Strait crossing from the South Island to the North Island, heading up to the bridge to meet the captain, before enjoying a sunny beer-tasting out on deck
